title: A phylogenomic framework for avian feather lice (Phthiraptera: Ischnocera)
content:
Abstract
Comprehensive phylogenies serve as foundations for taxonomic, comparative, and coevolutionary studies. Avian feather lice compose the most diverse parvorder (Ischnocera) of parasitic lice (Phthiraptera). Convergence in ecomorphology and reduction of morphological features resulting from adaptation to parasitism in this group have made past attempts at understanding the evolutionary relationships of feather lice challenging. Several recent phylogenomic studies have begun to shed light on the broader-scale evolutionary tree of this group. However, additional taxonomic sampling is needed for a more complete understanding of the phylogeny and for higher statistical power in comparative studies. Here, we investigate the higher-level relationships of feather lice based on the most comprehensive taxon sample to date. We leverage genome sequences of 260 samples of feather lice and 25 outgroup taxa to reconstruct a phylogenomic tree based on 2395 target nuclear orthologue genes, using both concatenated and coalescent methods. These trees provide high support across nearly all branches of the topology, resolving backbone relationships, in addition to more detailed relationships within major groups. These phylogenies provide a framework for future comparative studies of feather lice, including comparisons with avian phylogeny and investigation of patterns of diversification.
